we propose a novel formulation for dense semantic 2D-3D reconstruction which is a convex relaxation augmented with an additional non-convex consistency constraint.

(1) a non-convex visibility constraint is crucial in the formulation of the data term for semantic 3D reconstructions and (2) our approach sets a new state-of-the-art for geometry reconstruction and dense semantic 3d reconstruction.

the following questions: 1.

our method is a general-purpose approach for 3D reconstruction that is able to handle thin objects and that is robust with respect to noise.
we propose the first method for dense semantic 2D-to-3D reconstruction that is both efficient and robust.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present the first method which can reconstruct thin objects, and which can handle visibility in a principled and exact way.
we provide a general-purpose method that is competitive with state-of-the-art methods for both the geometry-only and the semantic reconstruction problem.
we provide a general and efficient formulation which allows us to reconstruct thin objects and to perform dense semantic 3d reconstruction.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the visibility consistency constraint is essential for obtaining a dense and accurate reconstruction of both geometry and semantic information.
